source.application: Pre-commit working tree after 7cfedb4; only production Secret transport changed

behavior.retryOnly: Locally detected oversized successful full-list GET body; only while page limit exceeds one
behavior.budgets: Four-MiB individual response; shared 32-MiB delivered response-body bytes including rejected prefixes, 10,000 accepted objects and 15 seconds across selected namespaces
behavior.failures: Single over-cap object at limit one, aggregate exhaustion, cursor repeat/empty advancement, malformed kind/count/map all fail closed; no partial success
behavior.contract: Exact key names/type/immutable/namespace/name/RV and public value/annotation withholding remain unchanged; TLS/CAS/fresh value permissions unchanged

focusedProofs: Small ordinary pages retain 20-object batching; 40 objects require two requests
Oversize at a continuation cursor retries that same cursor; 45 mixed records remain distinct and complete
Rejected prefix bytes exceed four MiB and remain counted with accepted bytes
25 256-KiB flat records plus 99 other namespaces project under one budget through 103 requests, without returning full objects
Three one-MiB decoded flat records remain usable through limits 20/10/5/2/2
An adversarial individually over-cap object fails after exactly five attempts, through limits 20/10/5/2/1
Aggregate byte/item/deadline exhaustion stops later namespace work and clears the pool
Owned maximum-size history GC remains metadata-only with ownership/source/UID/RV fences

controlledLinux.runtime: Node 22.23.3 in existing local QA base; no final application image built
controlledLinux.method: Verified loopback TLS mock API in separate process; fresh measured client per case; alternating baseline/adaptive; three repetitions per mode/case; fixed 12-ms producer delay; reset synthetic identity and assert repeat fixture size

interpretation.small334: Requests 334 to 18 and median 4965.27 to 279.58 ms; received response-body bytes 103828 to 79342. Controlled synthetic improvement, not live latency acceptance.
interpretation.maximumKv25: Requests 25 to 4 and median 469.72 to 188.76 ms, but received bytes rise from 8.75 to 12.95 MB and client high-water rises from 182-184 to 188-190 MiB.
interpretation.maximumFlat3: Requests 3 to 5 and median 90.75 to 231.71 ms; received bytes rise from 4.20 to 16.78 MB and client high-water from 171-176 to 190-199 MiB. Large-record retries cost latency, CPU, transfer and memory; they can exhaust a collection budget earlier.
interpretation.historyMetadata25: One metadata-only request in both readers; values remain absent. Its separate eight-MiB metadata bound is unchanged; receivedBodyBytes=0 because the full-list budget is not used for this negotiated path.
interpretation.memory: 24 measured clients completed under a one-GiB cgroup; combined cgroup peak 320159744 bytes. Process memory is not bounded by the 32-MiB received-body ceiling. No general RSS improvement claim.

corrections: Initial comparison completed but synthetic IDs continued increasing across cases, slightly varying payload sizes. Reset/size assertion was added; initial raw evidence is retained and corrected runs qualify the final comparison.

Post-reset harness typecheck rejected an inferred results array; explicit result types fixed it. Zero-warning lint/typecheck and six focused tests subsequently passed. Type-only correction does not change measured runtime behavior.
reproduction: Use tests/qualify-secret-capacity.ts in a disposable Linux source/dependency snapshot, with baseline-lib copied from 7cfedb4 src/lib and current src/lib overlaid. Generate Prisma in that owned snapshot, use a TLS-fixture-capable Node22 base with OpenSSL, and run read-only under the documented limits. Never mount operator env/DB/kubeconfig.
limitations: Synthetic 334-object/18-namespace count is derived from the reported baseline, not refreshed live inventory
Container quota and process separation control bounds; shared host/VM scheduling, warm kernel cache and cold module/TLS state still influence results
Cgroup counters include parent/mock API/client/cache; per-client proc high-water includes imports and allocations, not only list buffers
No production limits, live credentials, DB, deployments, admission or RBAC changed
Metadata-only requests never fall back to full Secret bodies; Table remains a future explicit caller migration
A21 DOM bounds/full-server CPU/RSS, A22 browser/live latency and final compatible image/recovery acceptance remain open
